function.name: ecology_get_turtle_population
function.description: Get the population and species of turtles in a specific location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

year.description: The year of the data requested. (optional). default is 2000

species.description: Whether to include species information. Default is false. (optional)

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "2015年加拉巴哥群島的龜類人口是多少，您能提供物種訊息嗎？之後，您也能告訴我同一地點2020年的相同物種訊息嗎？" They want the turtle population in Galapagos Islands in 2015 with species info, then also the same species info for 2020.

We have a tool function ecology_get_turtle_population that can get population and species. It takes location, optional year, optional species flag. We need to call it twice: once for 2015 with species true, once for 2020 with species true. Then we need to format the answer nicely.

We should use the function calls. We'll do two calls. Use the function name "ecology_get_turtle_population". Provide location "Galapagos Islands", year 2015, species true. Then second call with year 2020. Then combine results.

We need to output the function calls as JSON objects. According to guidelines, we should produce separate messages for each function call? Actually guidelines say: "When you want to call a function, respond with a JSON object containing the name of the function and arguments." So we need to send a single function call? But we need two calls. We can chain them: first call, then after receiving result, call again. But we can't do both at once. We need to call one, wait for response, then call next. So we will first call for 2015. Then after receiving result, call for 2020. Then combine.

Thus step 1: call function for 2015.
